**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not gate default builds on known conformance failures**

Both Jenkins benchmark stages invoke this script with W3C conformance enabled, `run_benchmarks.ps1` throws whenever any case fails, and `runWithJenkinsTestResult` rethrows that failure. Since `RUN_BENCHMARKS` defaults to true and this commit’s own integration results in `docs/w3c-xml-conformance.md` record hundreds of wrong verdicts plus 1,360 assertion-build runtime errors, every default run of both inspected pipelines will fail until those parser gaps are fixed; make this known-red suite non-gating or opt-in, or introduce an explicit expected-failure baseline.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

| Exit status | **1** (rerun, `powershell -File` exit code). Original run: stopped at the same `throw`; exact code not recorded. |

Expectations for the reruns were written to a file at 2026-10-20 00:39, before running anything. For the original run (2026-10-19) the expectation was not written down beforehand; it is recorded here afterwards.

## Error output: original run, 2026-10-19 (full, as pasted)

```text
.\scripts\build_native_eiffel.ps1

+     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : OperationStopped: (Cannot find Eif...lude directory.:String) [], RuntimeExcepti
   on
FullyQualifiedErrorId : Cannot find Eiffel runtime include directory.
```

## Observations
- `Get-IseInclude` (`scripts/build_native_eiffel.ps1:35-47`) checks `$env:ISE_EIFFEL\studio\spec\win64\include`, then a hard-coded `C:\El2502E\studio\spec\win64\include`.
- `ISE_EIFFEL` is not set (user, machine and process) and `C:\El2502E` does not exist.
- The directory exists at `C:\Program Files\Eiffel Software\EiffelStudio 25.12 Standard\studio\spec\win64\include`, and `ec` is on PATH.
- The `'vswhere.exe' is not recognized` lines in the rerun come from `vcvars64.bat` and are harmless at this point (see #7).

## Cause (confirmed)
The fallback path belongs to a different install (EiffelStudio 25.02 Enterprise). With `ISE_EIFFEL` unset, neither location exists.

## Status
Fixed on `student-Mass` in 9eb18bd (fallback set to the 25.12 Standard install). With that fix the build gets past this step and stops at #7. Fix report: [reports/fix-report-issue-2.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/student-Mass/reports/fix-report-issue-2.md). Kept open until the fix reaches `main`.

## Logs
- Rerun output: above
- Original report: [reports/error-report-2026-10-19.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/student-Mass/reports/error-report-2026-10-19.md), error 1

Fix report with all four options considered and the verification run: [reports/fix-report-issue-2.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/student-Mass/reports/fix-report-issue-2.md)

**Verification:** with `ISE_EIFFEL` unset, the include-directory error no longer appears. The build then stops at the known `'vswhere.exe' is not recognized` stderr error (`build_native_eiffel.ps1:52`), which is not part of this issue; see the "Next blocker" section of the report.

Leaving this open until the fix reaches `main`. A more portable fix (searching the install folders, option 4) is suggested for that.

Expectations for the reruns were written to a file at 2026-10-20 00:39, before running anything. For the original run (2026-10-19) the expectation was not written down beforehand; it is recorded here afterwards.

The call that fails (`tests/xp_test_root.e:1069-1072`), with GC collection on before the call:

```eiffel
l_memory.collection_on
create l_native.make
l_native.set_suspend_gc_during_parse (True)
l_status := l_native.parse ("<root/>", True)
```

comments.body:
**B03 answer: the contract is wrong, not the code or the test.** Fix proposed in #12, **waiting for review by the parser's developer** (not merged).

**Root cause:** the outer loop variant `a_end_index - i` in `XP_NATIVE_PARSER.direct_start_tag_attributes` does not decrease when an iteration only sets `l_valid := False` without advancing `i`, as at the `/` of `<root/>`. With assertions on, the runtime raises "Non-decreasing loop variant". The loop itself terminates correctly.

**Why it looked like `final_finished_or_suspended`:** with GC suspension on, the parse runs inside `MEMORY.execute_without_collection`, whose `rescue ... retry` silently swallows the variant exception. The parse is abandoned and the outer postcondition of `parse` fails instead. Reported separately as #13.

**How it was found** (throwaway worktree, nothing committed):
1. Removed the swallowing rescue → the real exception appeared: `direct_start_tag_attributes`, "Non-decreasing loop variant".
2. Turned GC suspension off in the test → same failure, so it is **not GC-related**.

**Fix (#12):** variant → `a_end_index - i + l_valid.to_integer`. Behaviour unchanged, check stays on.

**Verification on the fix branch** (each cell in a fresh process, expectations written before testing):

| Cell | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| On / Workbench | postcondition failure, exit 1 | "xpact Phase 1 tests: ok", **exit 0** |
| On / Finalized | not reached | ok, **exit 0** |
| Off / Workbench | (exit code not trusted) | ok, exit 0 |
| Off / Finalized | (exit code not trusted) | ok, exit 0 |

No other test failed after this one, although those tests had never run with assertions on before.

Fix report with the analysis, proof of the new variant and all logs: [reports/fix-report-issue-3.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/d9f662f6c5455a09865124ff8b38f2092979a8c2/reports/fix-report-issue-3.md)

**New evidence, 2026-10-22 (through the DLL, #37).** B03 does not only break the GC-suspension test: it crashes `xpact_assertions.dll` on **every input with `/>`**, including `<root/>` itself.

| `xpact_assertions.dll` | whole-document crashes | all crashes | crashes without a trace |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| current `student-Mass` (`42d6b40`) | 86 (84 of them inputs with `/>`) | 1,329 | 811 |
| `42d6b40` + **only** the B03 line from `d9f662f` | 2 (both #28) | 672 | 158 |

- **Confirmed:** with only the B03 change, no `/>` input crashes any more (`<root/>`, `<root/>junk`, all attribute and element-name cases).
- Most of these crashes print **no Eiffel trace** (the process just ends with `0xC0000409`); a few show `XP_NATIVE_PARSER direct_start_tag_attributes @11 a_end_index - i: Non-decreasing loop variant`. Losing the trace fits #13.
- The C smoke test `xpact_assertions_eiffel_dll_smoke.exe` **still crashes** (`0xC0000028`) with the B03 fix, so B03 is not the only cause of K3 (draft 07).

How it was done: separate worktree `C:\xpact\xpact-b03-check` at `42d6b40`, `git show d9f662f -- src | git apply`, `scripts\build_native_eiffel.ps1 -BuildTier Assertions -OutputDir build\native-eiffel-b03`; nothing committed. Details: [results README, finding 4](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/README.md#findings) · [diff](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/assertions-b03fix/b03-fix.diff) · [build log](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/assertions-b03fix/build.log) · [crash example](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/assertions/crash-examples/b03-no-trace-c02-valid_none_whole.txt)

## Observations
- PATH length: 1,335 at start → 2,767 → 4,199 → 5,631 → 7,063 after 4 imports (+1,432 each).
- The 5th import fails: `vcvars64.bat` itself prints "The input line is too long." once PATH plus what it prepends passes cmd.exe's ~8,191-character limit.
- `import_msvc_environment.ps1` copies the whole vcvars environment into the process with `Set-Item Env:...`, so every script in the same window that imports it adds another copy of the Visual Studio folders.

## Cause (confirmed by the rerun)
Repeated imports in one PowerShell process grow PATH until `vcvars64.bat` exceeds cmd.exe's line limit.

## Workaround and known fix
- **Workaround:** run each script in a new PowerShell window.
- **Fix (exists in another local copy, `xpactVsCode\xpact\scripts\import_msvc_environment.ps1`):** skip the import when `VSCMD_VER` is set and `cl.exe` is found, and de-duplicate PATH when importing.
- `build_native_eiffel.ps1` also runs `vcvars64.bat` again for every `cl`/`link` call (`Invoke-VcCommand`), starting from the already-long PATH.

issue.body:
## Goal
Many fixes (several hundred pushes) will go to `student-Mass`. Each fix must be:
- **traceable**: linked to an issue, with the reason recorded
- **tested**: the evidence is committed next to the fix
- **easy to revert**: one commit undoes it, without rewriting history

## Plan
- `student/VERSIONING.md`: the rules and the step-by-step workflow
- `student/tools/fix.ps1`: `start`, `finish`, `merge`, `revert`, `status`
  - one branch per fix, `fix/<issue>-<name>`, from the latest `student-Mass`
  - `finish` checks that every commit names the issue and that `reports/fix-report-issue-<n>.md` has a `## Verification` section, then opens a pull request
  - `merge` squash-merges, so each fix is one commit on `student-Mass`
- `student/git/commit-template.txt`: commit message template asking for `Refs #<issue>`

issue.body:
## Report details

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Git commit | **Rerun:** `cada501ca3117135d3649e1e8ca45b2ccc717748` (`student-Mass`, includes the #2 fix; git clone, exact). **Original run** (2026-10-20): copied folder `xpact3.0\...` with the #2 fix applied by hand, not a git clone, most likely `4f71743`. |
| Input file / SHA-256 | n/a: build failure, no XML is parsed |
| Exact command | `.\scripts\build_native_eiffel.ps1` (defaults: `-BuildTier Production -OutputDir build\native-eiffel`). Rerun as `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build_native_eiffel.ps1`, with `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer` added to the front of PATH (see Observations) |
| Compiler versions | EiffelStudio 25.12.9.8922 win64 · Visual Studio 18 Community 18.10.3, MSVC 14.51.36231 · Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300 · Windows PowerShell 5.1. **Eiffel C backend used: mingw** (`gcc` from the EiffelStudio install); `ISE_C_COMPILER` not set (user, machine, process) |
| Assertions / build mode | Production tier: target `xpact_native_library`, assertions **off** (all six off in `tests/xpact_native_library.ecf`), **Finalized** (`ec -batch -clean -finalize -keep`) |
| Loaded library | None: no DLL was built (`build\native-eiffel` contains only the three `.obj` files) |
| Callbacks | n/a (no parse) |
| Chunk sizes | n/a (no parse) |
| Expected | `build\native-eiffel\xpact.dll` is built and the smoke test passes |
| Actual | `ec` and `finish_freezing` finish ("C compilation completed"), then `Get-LinkResponseFile` throws: no `xpact_native_library.lnk` in `F_code` |
| Exit status | **1** (rerun). Original run: stopped at the same `throw` (`build_native_eiffel.ps1:91`); exact code not recorded. |

Expectations for the reruns were written to a file at 2026-10-20 00:39 (and, for the PATH variant, again before that run). For the original run the expectation was not written down beforehand.

## Observations
- The full log shows **"Preparing C compilation using already configured mingw C compiler..."**, and every C file is compiled with `...\EiffelStudio 25.12 Standard\gcc\win64\mingw\bin\gcc`.
- After the run, `EIFGENs\xpact_native_library\F_code` contains `Makefile`, `Makefile.SH` and `xpact_native_library.exe`, and **no `.lnk` file**.
- `Get-LinkResponseFile` (`scripts/build_native_eiffel.ps1:78-92`) needs `F_code\<target>.lnk`, or exactly one other `*.lnk`, which only an MSVC backend writes.
- **The same command without the PATH change stops earlier:** in a fresh `powershell -File` process, `Invoke-VcCommand` (line 52, `cmd.exe /c ... 2>&1`) turns the `'vswhere.exe' is not recognized` stderr line from `vcvars64.bat` into a terminating error, exit 1 after 1 s. ## Cause (confirmed by the rerun)
EiffelStudio's configured C backend on this PC is **mingw**. It links with gcc and writes no `.lnk` response file, but the script expects the MSVC link step.

## Known fix (from week 1, not yet applied)
From `student/history/xpact-error-report.md` §4.1-4.4, in `student/history/patches/01-week1-build-fixes.patch` (commit `b930600`):
- Set `ISE_C_COMPILER = "msc_vc140"` around the `ec` and `finish_freezing` calls. (The plain `msc` backend failed with VS 18: unresolved `__iob_func`, `_set_output_format`.)
- Remove the mingw-only `<precompile>` from both targets in `tests/xpact_native_library.ecf` (lines 18 and 37).
- Delete a stale `EIFGENs\xpact_native_library\ec.lock` if one is left.
- Guard native calls against stderr (the `vswhere.exe` problem above).

Related: #2 (previous step in the same script), #4 (MSVC environment import).

Build the native Eiffel library with the msc_vc140 C backend

EiffelStudio's default C backend on this PC is mingw, which writes no
.lnk link response file, so build_native_eiffel.ps1 stopped with
"Expected Eiffel link response file not found". Compile the target with
ISE_C_COMPILER=msc_vc140 (restored afterwards), drop the mingw-only
precompiled base from xpact_native_library.ecf, and keep harmless
stderr from vcvars64.bat from aborting native commands.

This is the week 1 fix (patch 01, commit b930600) for these two files.
Verified: Production DLL builds and its smoke test passes, Assertions
DLL builds, exit 0 in a fresh process; see reports/fix-report-issue-7.md.

commit.message:
Stop repeated MSVC imports from growing PATH past cmd's limit

Every script dot-sources import_msvc_environment.ps1, and each import
prepended another copy of the Visual Studio folders to PATH, so the 5th
import in one window failed with "The input line is too long." Skip the
import when an x64 MSVC environment is already loaded, and drop
duplicate PATH entries when importing.

Verified: 20 imports in one process succeed with PATH fixed at 2,657
characters (before: import 5 failed), and two native builds in one
process both succeed; see reports/fix-report-issue-4.md.

Refs #4

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## Observations
- **A:** `Get-IseInclude` (`scripts/run_native_runtime_smoke.ps1:33-45`) has the same `C:\El2502E` fallback that #2 fixed in `build_native_eiffel.ps1`.
- **B:**

  - It linked with `gcc` against the mingw precompiled library `...\precomp\spec\win64\EIFGENs\base-safe\W_code\mingw\precomp.lib`.
  - `xpact_native.obj` and `xpact_eiffel_runtime_bridge.obj` were compiled by MSVC `cl` (`Compile-CObject`). They reference MSVC CRT symbols that the mingw linker can't resolve.
- Same root cause as #7: the Eiffel part is built with mingw, but the native objects are MSVC. `tests/xpact_native_runtime.ecf` also uses the mingw-only `<precompile>` in both targets.
- Like #7 before its fix, `ec`, `finish_freezing` and the smoke `.exe` run under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` with no stderr guard.

- Use the 25.12 Standard install as the include fallback.
- Run `ec`/`finish_freezing` with `ISE_C_COMPILER=msc_vc140`, restored afterwards.
- Guard native commands against stderr.
- Remove `<precompile>` from both targets.

This is the same fix as #2 and #7 (pull request #8), applied to this script.

Related: #2, #7.

commit.message:
Fix the loop variant in direct_start_tag_attributes (B03)

The outer loop's variant a_end_index - i does not decrease when an
iteration only sets l_valid to False, as at the '/' of "<root/>", so
with assertions on the runtime raised "Non-decreasing loop variant".
Under GC suspension MEMORY.execute_without_collection swallowed that
exception, which surfaced as the final_finished_or_suspended
postcondition failure in test_garbage_collection_suspension.

Count the l_valid exit as progress: a_end_index - i +
l_valid.to_integer. Behaviour is unchanged and the check stays on.

Verified: all four test matrix cells print "xpact Phase 1 tests: ok",
exit 0; see reports/fix-report-issue-3.md for the diagnostics.

Refs #3

milestone.title: Week 2 - Baseline
milestone.description: Follow parser events and run the assertions-enabled tests. Baseline log with revision, configuration, commands and known failures.

issue.body:
## Report details

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Git commit | `20e6bc3` on `student-Mass` (git clone, exact) |
| Input file / SHA-256 | No file: the literal `<root/>` (7 bytes) in `tests/xp_test_root.e:1072`, SHA-256 `6238462c4873df4c50bc1a901ece576b2d166b0156802c88a05a85b1f5d511c7` |
| Exact command | `.\scripts\run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1 -AssertionMode On -BuildMode Workbench`; diagnostic runs in a throwaway worktree with the change in the Logs section |
| Compiler versions | EiffelStudio 25.12.9.8922 win64 · Visual Studio 18 Community 18.10.3, MSVC 14.51.36231 · Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300 · Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| Assertions / build mode | Assertions On, Workbench |
| Loaded library | None (`xpact_tests.exe` is a plain Eiffel program) |
| Callbacks | None (`XP_NATIVE_PARSER` created with `make`) |
| Chunk sizes | Whole document, `is_final = True` |
| Expected | An exception raised inside a GC-suspended parse reaches the caller, so the trace names the real failure |
| Actual | The exception is silently dropped. The parse returns `Xml_status_error` with `parsing_status` unchanged, and the only visible symptom is a different, misleading failure (#3: `final_finished_or_suspended`) |
| Exit status | 1 (from the misleading postcondition failure) |

## Cause

`XP_GC_CRITICAL_SECTION.execute` (`src/xp_gc_critical_section.e:80-88`) calls `MEMORY.execute_without_collection` from EiffelStudio's base library (`library/base/elks/kernel/memory.e:306-338`). That routine ends with:

```eiffel
rescue
    retried := True
    retry
end
```

So any exception in the action (contract violation, Void call, I/O error, ...) is caught, collection is restored, and the routine returns normally, as if the action had succeeded.

`XP_NATIVE_PARSER.parse` uses this for every parse with `suspend_gc_during_parse = True` (`src/xp_native_parser.e:745-749`). `XP_PARSER.parse_without_garbage_collection` (`src/xp_parser.e:363-375`) uses the same path, so an exception there becomes a plain `False` result.

## Evidence

In #3 the real exception was a loop-variant violation in `direct_start_tag_attributes` (fixed for review in #12). The test only showed the outer postcondition `final_finished_or_suspended` of `parse`, because the variant exception was swallowed. Replacing `memory.execute_without_collection (a_action)` with `enter; a_action.call (Void); leave` (diagnostic only, not committed) made the real exception appear:

```text
XP_NATIVE_PARSER    direct_start_tag_attributes @11
                    a_end_index - i: Non-decreasing loop variant or negative value reached.
...
XP_GC_CRITICAL_SECTION execute @3
XP_NATIVE_PARSER    parse @5
```

Full logs: `reports/fix-issue-3-diagnostic-no-rescue.txt` and `reports/fix-issue-3-diagnostic.diff.txt` on branch `fix/3-start-tag-loop-variant` (#12).

## Why it matters

- In assertions-on builds, real contract violations inside GC-suspended parses are hidden or show up as unrelated failures.
- In assertions-off and production builds, the parse fails with `Xml_status_error` but the cause is lost, and the parser can be left half-updated (`parsing_status`, buffers).

## Possible fix (not implemented, needs review: it changes library behaviour)

Implement `execute` without `execute_without_collection`: `enter`, call the action, `leave`, and in a `rescue` clause call `leave` (if active) and let the exception propagate (no `retry`). The postcondition `collection_status_preserved` still holds on normal exit. Add a test where the action raises, checking that the exception reaches the caller and that collection is restored.

Related: #3, #12.

comments.body:
**Possibly related, 2026-10-22 (#37):** through `xpact_assertions.dll`, many contract failures end the process with `0xC0000409` and **no Eiffel trace at all**, while others of the same kind print a full trace. Whether a given case prints a trace is not even stable: 17 of 1,329 crashes had a trace in one run and none in the next.

- 811 of 1,329 crashes without a trace on the current DLL; most are B03 (#3), and they disappear with the B03 fix.
- With the B03 fix, 132 crashes without a trace remain, all with the same trigger as #40 (a chunk ending with `<`), where other cases show `find_markup_declaration_end index_in_bounds`.

That the trace is lost the way this issue describes (an exception swallowed during a GC-suspended parse) is **suspected**, not shown. Data: [results README](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/README.md#repeatability-).

issue.body:
## Goal

Give every fix its own folder under `reports/` so the folder stays readable for the ~500 fixes planned:

```
reports/
  README.md            index of all fixes: issue, title, pull request, merged commit
  error-reports/       dated error reports (not tied to one fix)
  issue-0007/
    report.md          the fix report, with ## Verification
    *.txt              logs and test scripts for that fix
```

## Why

`reports/` is a flat list today: 18 files for 5 fixes (`fix-report-issue-N.md` plus `fix-issue-N-*.txt`).

- Names sort as text, so issue 10 is listed before issue 2.
- At ~4 files per fix, 500 fixes would be ~2,000 files in one folder. GitHub's folder view truncates at 1,000 entries.
- Nothing groups one fix's report with its evidence except a name prefix.

## Done when

- [x] Existing files moved with `git mv` (history kept), links inside the reports updated _(verified 2026-10-22 at `76ac272`)_
- [x] `student/tools/fix.ps1`: `finish` checks `reports/issue-NNNN/report.md`; `start` creates the folder _(verified 2026-10-22 at `76ac272`)_
- [x] `student/VERSIONING.md` rule 5 and the examples use the new paths _(verified 2026-10-22 at `76ac272`)_
- [x] `reports/README.md` lists every fix _(verified 2026-10-22 at `76ac272`)_
- [x] Verification in `reports/issue-NNNN/report.md` for this issue _(verified 2026-10-22 at `76ac272`)_

## Goal
Week 3 moved every fix to `reports/issue-NNNN/` with the `fix.ps1` workflow, but several documents still describe the week 2 setup, and some week 3 results are missing. Nothing should be in one place and missing from another.

## Missing
- `student/notes/weekly/week-03.md` (PLAN.md lists it as a to-do)
- `reports/error-reports/2026-10-19.md`: no outcome section; errors 2 and 3 still say "not confirmed" although #4 fixed error 3 and #3 found error 2's cause
- `reports/README.md`: #18 row has no commit (`df189d9`)

## Out of date
- `student/README.md`: "PLAN.md is the empty version"; layout without `reports/`, `VERSIONING.md`, `tools/`; branch names and steps from before `fix.ps1`; "Closes #N" (does not close issues for pull requests into `student-Mass`)
- `student/results/README.md`: "one folder per issue" competes with `reports/issue-NNNN/`
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`: evidence in `student/results/`, "Closes #"
- `student/baseline/BASELINE.md`: K1 status (B03 root cause #3, #12, #13); §1 points at the deleted `student-test` branch
- `student/baseline/README.md` and `student/history/README.md`: "apply the patches" (most of patch 01 is now in git as #2, #7, #10); wrong clone path
- `student/github/README.md`: wrong clone path; drafts that are already issues
- `student/PLAN.md`: last-updated commit

## Risk
`student/github/setup-github.ps1` skips a draft only if an issue with exactly the same title exists. Draft `05-finding-b03-postcondition.md` has a different title from #3, so running the script would create a duplicate B03 issue.

milestone.description: How the test runner reports failure; a deliberately failing test (B01, B02). A bounded fix or a precise proposal with evidence.

issue.body:
## Report details

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Git commit | `2f0d441633fe036fabf0d972aa68c5e3836c60cd` (`student-Mass`, git clone, no local changes in `src/`, `benchmarks/`, `scripts/`) |
| Input file / SHA-256 | `cr-lf.xml`, 9 bytes `3C 72 3E 0D 0A 3C 2F 72 3E` (`<r>` CR LF `</r>`), SHA-256 `5b7e3147871965a78cccb9a0693be825766ba0125de44acf6f21debcff2a9fed`. Control: `lf.xml`, same without the CR (8 bytes), SHA-256 `7b5783c08d18f9276eea591b0e50210fd77f15d18f829097a98333654d4881c5` |
| Exact command | `EIFGENs\xpact_benchmarks_assertions\F_code\xpact_benchmarks.exe --conformance-file cr-lf.xml` |
| Compiler versions | EiffelStudio 25.12.9.8922 win64 · Visual Studio 18 Community, MSVC 14.51.36231 · Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 · Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| Assertions / build mode | Assertions **On**: `benchmarks/xpact_benchmarks.ecf` target `xpact_benchmarks_assertions` (all assertion kinds true), `ec -batch -clean -finalize -keep`, then `finish_freezing` |
| Loaded library | None: `xpact_benchmarks.exe` is a plain Eiffel program; `--conformance-file` calls `XP_PARSER.parse` directly (`benchmarks/xp_benchmark_root.e:63-68`) |
| Callbacks | `XP_NULL_EVENT_HANDLER` (no-op) |
| Chunk sizes | Whole document in one call |
| Expected | `XPACT_CONFORMANCE	ACCEPT`, exit 0 (the document is well formed) |
| Actual | Loop variant violation in `XP_PARSER.normalized_input`, exit 1 |
| Exit status | **1** |

| Input | Assertions off (`xpact_benchmarks`) | Assertions on (`xpact_benchmarks_assertions`) |
|---|---|---|
| `lf.xml` | ACCEPT, exit 0 | ACCEPT, exit 0 |
| `cr-lf.xml` | ACCEPT, exit 0 | **crash, exit 1** |

## Error output

```text
xpact_benchmarks: system execution failed.
Following is the set of recorded exceptions:

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Class / Object      Routine                Nature of exception           Effect
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XP_PARSER           normalized_input @8    a_input.count - i + 1:
<0000027FD2042808>                         Non-decreasing loop variant or negative value reached.
                                                                         Fail
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XP_PARSER           normalized_input @8
<0000027FD2042808>                         Routine failure.              Fail
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XP_PARSER           parse @5
<0000027FD2042808>                         Routine failure.              Fail
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XP_BENCHMARK_ROOT   run_conformance @24
<0000027FD2041588>                         Routine failure.              Fail
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XP_BENCHMARK_ROOT   make @2
<0000027FD2041588>                         Routine failure.              Fail
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XP_BENCHMARK_ROOT   root's creation
<0000027FD2041588>                         Routine failure.              Exit
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

(Trace from W3C case `not-wf-sa-001`; the 9-byte input gives the same first entry.)

## Observations

- The loop is `src/xp_parser.e:4461-4478`, in the `a_allow_alias` branch of `normalized_input`:

  ```eiffel
  until
      i > a_input.count or has_error or l_needs_copy
  loop
      c := a_input.item (i)
      if c = '%R' then
          l_needs_copy := True        -- i is not changed
      elseif not is_xml_character_code (c.code) then
          set_error ("invalid XML character")
          i := a_input.count + 1
      else
          i := i + 1
      end
  variant
      a_input.count - i + 1
  end
  ```

  When `c = '%R'`, `l_needs_copy` becomes True but `i` is not changed, so the variant does not decrease in that iteration. The exit condition (`l_needs_copy`) still ends the loop, so without assertions the result is correct.
- W3C suite 20130923 with `scripts/run_w3c_conformance.py`, 1,727 applicable cases: with assertions on, **1,357 cases crash here**. All 1,357 files contain a CR byte (0x0D); no file without CR crashes here. With assertions off, the same build has 0 crashes.
- Because almost every W3C file has CR LF line ends, this hides any other assertion failure in the suite. The 53-crash finding from 2026-10-14 (`student/github/issues/21-finding-xmlconf-crashes.md`) cannot be rechecked until this is fixed.
- Same kind of failure as B03 (#3): a loop variant that does not decrease although the loop ends correctly.

## Possible explanation (not confirmed)

The variant does not account for the `l_needs_copy` exit. Either `i` should also advance on CR, or the variant should also decrease when `l_needs_copy` becomes True. Choosing the repair is for the developers; the contract has not been switched off.

## Logs

The W3C run, the 9-byte inputs and the crash list are committed under `student/results/w3c-conformance-2026-10-21/` with the W3C run task.

comments.body: The repro and the W3C evidence are now on student-Mass (8850dab, #30): student/results/w3c-conformance-2026-10-21/ (cr-lf.xml, lf.xml, failures.tsv with all 1,357 cases) and reports/error-reports/2026-10-21.md, error 1.

Regression test added on student-Mass in 1ea242e (test_cr_line_ends_with_deferred_positions). It fails with assertions on until the parser is repaired; a one-line repair is proposed in reports/issue-0028/report.md for the parser's developers. Leaving this issue open.

**Also through the DLL, 2026-10-22 (#37):** with **no callbacks set**, CR LF, a lone CR, a CR after the root and a CR in an attribute crash `xpact_assertions.dll` (whole document: `cr-crlf/none/whole`, `cr-lone/none/whole`, …). With the B03 fix applied, the trace shows this bug:

```
XP_PARSER  normalized_input @8  a_input.count - i + 1: Non-decreasing loop variant or negative value reached.
```

With **any** callback set the same inputs pass, and the character data is a single LF (`text:\x0a`), exactly as the analysis in `reports/issue-0028/report.md` predicts (only a handler that wants no events reaches the broken loop). 28 crashes of this kind on the B03-fixed DLL.

Data: [results README, finding 5](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/README.md#findings) · [crash example](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/assertions-b03fix/crash-examples/cr-28-cr-crlf_none_whole.txt). Still open: the parser is not repaired.

Repaired in `d279717` (PR #59). Regression test passes with assertions on; W3C with assertions on: crashes 1,360 -> 47 (the rest are in DTD declaration parsing, listed in reports/issue-0028/w3c-after-fix/).

milestone.description: Small inputs with different callbacks and chunk boundaries (C02, C03, C10). Repeatable regressions and bug reproductions.

issue.body:
**1. Problem:** with a start-element handler set, xpact accepts documents that are not well-formed, and with start and end handlers set it does not deliver the end event of a valid document. The expected behaviour is C01 in the task register: "An emitted start event must never substitute for parsing the remaining input."

**2. Environment:** Windows 11, `student-Mass` @ `42d6b40` (parser), `xpact.dll` (assertions off, SHA-256 `62a2706b…`), `xpact_assertions.dll` (`8cc96794…`) and the same with the B03 fix (`38c2b2c7…`). Same result on all three.

**3. Command:**
```powershell
dotnet build tests\dotnet\XpactDllTests -c Release
build\dotnet\XpactDllTests\bin\Release\net10.0\XpactDllTests.exe --dll build\native-eiffel\xpact.dll --group c02 --verbose
```
Program from #37. One case: `--only c02-incomplete/start/whole --verbose --isolate`.

**4. Expected:** `<root>` and `<root><child></root>` REJECT with every callback set; `<root></root>` ACCEPT with the events `start:root`, `end:root`.

**5. Actual** (`xpact.dll`):

| Case | Result | Events |
|---|---|---|
| `c02-incomplete/start/whole` (`<root>`) | **ACCEPT** | `start:root` |
| `c02-mismatched/start+end/whole` (`<root><child></root>`) | **ACCEPT** | `start:root` |
| `c02-valid-pair/start+end/whole` (`<root></root>`) | ACCEPT | `start:root` (**no** `end:root`) |
| the same inputs with `none`, `end`, `chardata`, `default` | right | right |
| the same inputs, `start+end/bytes` (byte by byte) | right | right |

24 wrong ACCEPTs and 30 missing end events in 3,360 cases.

**6. Error output:** none: `XML_Parse` returns `XML_STATUS_OK`.

**7. Investigation:** wrong only when (a) a start handler is set **and** (b) the **final** `XML_Parse` call is the one that completes the first start tag (whole document, or a split before the end of `<root>`). When the start tag is complete before the final call (byte by byte, later split points), the result is right. The assertions DLLs give the same wrong results, so no contract notices it.

**8. Cause:** **suspected:** the final-input prefix shortcut described in C01 (emit the start event, then return without validating the rest). Not confirmed in the code.

**9. Fix:** none. Parser change, for the parser's developers (task C01, D3).

**10. Verification:** a fix is verified when the `c02` group passes on `xpact_assertions.dll` for every callback set and chunking. A rerun gave the same result for every case.

**Logs:** [results README, finding 1](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/README.md#findings) · [production/results.tsv](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/production/results.tsv) · [production/summary.txt](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/production/summary.txt)

issue.body:
**1. Problem:** xpact accepts invalid UTF-8 in text, attribute values, element names, comments, processing instructions and CDATA. K4 of the week 2 baseline (`C3 28` in text) is one case of it.

**2. Environment:** Windows 11, `student-Mass` @ `42d6b40`, `xpact.dll` (assertions off, SHA-256 `62a2706b…`); the same on `xpact_assertions.dll` with the B03 fix (`38c2b2c7…`) wherever the case does not crash first.

**3. Command:**
```powershell
build\dotnet\XpactDllTests\bin\Release\net10.0\XpactDllTests.exe --dll build\native-eiffel\xpact.dll --group utf8
```
Program from #37. The inputs are exact bytes in the program (`Catalog.cs`), for example `<r>` `C3 28` `</r>`.

**4. Expected:** REJECT for `C3 28` (no continuation byte), `C0 AF` (overlong), `ED A0 80` (surrogate) and `F4 90 80 80` (above U+10FFFF), in each of the six places. ACCEPT for the control `C3 A9` (é).

**5. Actual:** **2,106 of 2,148** bad-sequence cases are ACCEPTED, with every callback set and chunking. The 42 rejected ones are all `C3 28` in an element name. The control `C3 A9` is accepted everywhere ✅.

| | text | attribute | name | comment | PI | CDATA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `C3 28` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | reject | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| `C0 AF` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| `ED A0 80` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |
| `F4 90 80 80` | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

**6. Error output:** none: `XML_Parse` returns `XML_STATUS_OK`, and the text callback receives the bad bytes unchanged (e.g. `text:\xc3(`).

**7. Investigation:** `C3 28` in a name is rejected because `(` is not a name character, so even that case does not show a UTF-8 check. The assertions DLL behaves the same: no contract checks UTF-8.

**8. Cause:** **suspected:** there is no strict UTF-8 decoder (task C08: "Reject bad continuations, overlong encodings, surrogates and values above U+10FFFF"). Not confirmed in the code.

**9. Fix:** none. Parser change (C08/C09, D3-D4), for the parser's developers.

**10. Verification:** a fix is verified when every bad-sequence case in the `utf8` group is REJECT and every `valid-e9` case still passes. A rerun gave the same result for every case.

**Logs:** [results README, finding 2](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/README.md#findings) · [production/results.tsv](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/production/results.tsv)

milestone.title: Week 5 - Regressions
milestone.description: Small inputs with different callbacks and chunk boundaries (C02, C03, C10). Repeatable regressions and bug reproductions.

issue.body:
**1. Problem:** a non-final `XML_Parse` call whose data ends with `<` crashes `xpact_assertions.dll`: an Eiffel loop invariant fails, the runtime panics, and the calling program dies with `0xC0000409`.

**2. Environment:** Windows 11, `student-Mass` @ `42d6b40`, `xpact_assertions.dll` from `build_native_eiffel.ps1 -BuildTier Assertions` (SHA-256 `8cc96794…`), and the same with only the B03 fix applied (`38c2b2c7…`). `xpact.dll` (assertions off) does not crash.

**3. Command:**
```powershell
build\dotnet\XpactDllTests\bin\Release\net10.0\XpactDllTests.exe --only c02-valid/none/split@1 --isolate --verbose
```
That is `XML_Parse(p, "<", 1, 0)` followed by `XML_Parse(p, "root/>", 6, 1)`, no callbacks. Program from #37.

**4. Expected:** ACCEPT, as for the whole document, with no contract violation.

**5. Actual:** the process ends with exit code `-1073740791` (`0xC0000409`) during the first call.

**6. Error output** (full output: [crash example](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/assertions-b03fix/crash-examples/lt-at-chunk-end-c02-valid_none_split_1.txt)):
```
xpact_native_library: PANIC: main entry point vanished ...
XP_PARSER           find_markup_declaration_end @4
                                           index_in_bounds:
                                           Loop invariant violated.      Fail
XP_PARSER           markup_prefix_end @18              Routine failure.
XP_PARSER           incomplete_markup_prefix_start @8  Routine failure.
XP_NATIVE_PARSER    should_defer_reparse_callbacks @9  Routine failure.
XP_NATIVE_PARSER    parse_with_current_gc_policy @26   Routine failure.
XP_NATIVE_PARSER    parse @7  ->  XP_NATIVE_BRIDGE_EXPORT parse @3  ->  XP_NATIVE_LIBRARY_ROOT
```

**7. Investigation:** with the B03 fix, all 672 crashes of the 3,360 cases were classified. **644** have `<` as the last byte of a non-final chunk (`split@1` of any input; splits right before `</r>`, `<!--`, `<?pi`, `<![CDATA[`; every byte-by-byte run). 512 of them show the trace above, **132 show no trace at all**. The other 28 are #28. Because every byte-by-byte run crashes, no byte-by-byte result on the assertions DLL means anything until this is fixed. Whether a crash prints a trace is not stable between runs (17 cases changed).

**8. Cause:** the trigger is **confirmed** (a chunk ends with `<`). In the code it is **suspected** that `find_markup_declaration_end` steps past the end of the available input when the markup so far is only `<`. That the 132 crashes without a trace have the same cause is also **suspected** (the trace may be lost, see #13).

**9. Fix:** none. Parser change, for the parser's developers.

**10. Verification:** a fix is verified when no `split` or `bytes` case crashes in `find_markup_declaration_end` on `xpact_assertions.dll`.

**Logs:** [results README, finding 3](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/README.md#findings) · [assertions-b03fix/results.tsv](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/assertions-b03fix/results.tsv) · [summary](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/37-dll-test-program/student/results/dll-tests-2026-10-22/assertions-b03fix/summary.txt)

Accumulated failures in the main and native runtime test runners must make the process exit nonzero, independently of Eiffel `check` instructions.

Student guide, "P0 reliable test and benchmark outcomes". A run that reports failures but exits 0 shows up as green in CI.

## Evidence / notes
Related findings: the missing `-keep` in the finalized lane, and the runner stopping at the first failure.

issue.body:
﻿## Steps to reproduce
1. `.\scripts\run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1 -AssertionMode On -BuildMode Finalized`
2. Compare with `ec -batch -clean -finalize -keep -config tests\xpact_tests.ecf -target xpact_tests_assertions`, then `finish_freezing` and run `xpact_tests.exe`

## Expected
Both runs check assertions and give the same result.

## Actual
In the baseline from 2026-10-14, step 1 reported "ok" (exit 0). Step 2, with `-keep`, failed with the same postcondition violation as the workbench lane. `run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1` calls `ec -finalize` **without `-keep`**, so the finalized binary has no assertions compiled in. The green result is misleading, also in CI.

## Logs
Original logs: `student/baseline/logs/matrix-finalized.log`, `matrix-finalized-keep.log`.
Attach `matrix-finalized.log` and `matrix-finalized-keep.log` from a rerun in this checkout.

## Proposed next step
Add `-keep` to the finalized lane, as `build_native_eiffel.ps1` already does. **This changes what CI reports, so discuss it with the supervisor before changing it.**

milestone.title: Week 3 - Failure reporting
milestone.description: How the test runner reports failure; a deliberately failing test (B01, B02). A bounded fix or a precise proposal with evidence.

issue.body:
## Steps to reproduce
1. Open Windows PowerShell 5.1 without the MSVC environment and without `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer` on `PATH`.
2. Run a script that loads MSVC with its output captured, e.g. `.\scripts\build_native_eiffel.ps1 *>&1 | Select -Last 5`, or `. .\scripts\import_msvc_environment.ps1` inside `& { ... } *>&1`.

## Expected
The MSVC environment is loaded and the script continues.

## Actual
`vcvars64.bat` calls `vswhere.exe` by name and prints `'vswhere.exe' is not recognized as an internal or external command` to stderr. With `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, Windows PowerShell 5.1 turns that into a `NativeCommandError` and the script stops in `import_msvc_environment.ps1` line 32. Seen again on 2026-10-22 when rebuilding the DLLs.

`import_msvc_environment.ps1` already knows where `vswhere.exe` is (`$VsWhere`), but does not put its folder on `PATH` for `vcvars64.bat`. Today the workaround is a manual first line in the setup guide (`student/report/setup-guide.md`, section 3), also noted in `student/PLAN.md` under "Workarounds in use".

## Proposed next step
Add the Installer folder to `PATH` inside the `cmd.exe` call that runs `vcvars64.bat`, then remove the manual step from the setup guide.

comments.body: Fixed in `3076a92` (PR #52).

issue.title: Put the VS Installer folder on PATH for vcvars64.bat
issue.body:
Refs #51

`vcvars64.bat` calls `vswhere.exe` by name; without `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer` on `PATH` it prints `'vswhere.exe' is not recognized` to stderr, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 stops `import_msvc_environment.ps1` when the output is captured. The script now appends that folder to `PATH` inside the `cmd.exe` call. The manual line in the setup guide is removed.

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Load MSVC with output captured, no Installer folder on `PATH` | `NativeCommandError`, exit 1 | loaded, `cl.exe` found, exit 0 |
| Load three times in one session | - | runs 2-3 skip ("already loaded"), `PATH` length unchanged (#4 still holds) |

milestone.description: How the test runner reports failure; a deliberately failing test (B01, B02). A bounded fix or a precise proposal with evidence.

issue.body:
## Steps to reproduce
1. Set `ISE_C_COMPILER=msc_vc140` (as the setup guide, section 2, says to) and open Windows PowerShell 5.1 without the MSVC environment loaded.
2. `.\scripts\run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1 -AssertionMode Off -BuildMode Workbench`

## Expected
The Workbench lane compiles, runs the tests and prints `xpact Eiffel test matrix: ok`.

## Actual
`run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1` loads MSVC only when a Finalized lane is selected (lines 86-88). A Workbench lane still runs `finish_freezing`, which with `msc_vc140` needs `cl`/`link`, so it fails: `finish_freezing failed for assertions-off / Workbench`, with no other explanation. First noted in `reports/issue-0028/report.md` ("How the lanes were run"); today worked around by loading MSVC by hand first (setup guide, section 3).

## Proposed next step
Load MSVC when a Finalized lane is selected (as now) **or** when `ISE_C_COMPILER` is an MSVC backend (`msc*`). Not unconditionally: with the default mingw backend the Workbench lane needs no MSVC, and machines without Visual Studio would otherwise fail.

milestone.title: Week 3 - Failure reporting
milestone.description: How the test runner reports failure; a deliberately failing test (B01, B02). A bounded fix or a precise proposal with evidence.

issue.body:
## Steps to reproduce
1. Have an old `EIFGENs\xpact_tests\W_code\xpact_tests.exe` in the repository root (any earlier Workbench run leaves one).
2. From **another folder**, run the script by its full path, e.g. `cd C:\somewhere; C:\...\xpact\scripts\run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1 -AssertionMode Off -BuildMode Workbench`

## Expected
The lane compiles and tests the current sources, or stops with an error.

## Actual
`ec -config tests\xpact_tests.ecf` resolves the ECF from the repository root (`$ConfigPath`), but writes `EIFGENs` into the **current folder**. The script then looks for `Makefile.SH` and `xpact_tests.exe` under `$RepoRoot\EIFGENs\...`: `finish_freezing` is skipped (no `Makefile.SH` there), the **old** `xpact_tests.exe` is run, and the script prints `xpact Eiffel test matrix: ok`, exit 0. A false pass, like #48. Seen on 2026-10-22 while testing #53 (`reports/issue-0053/report.md`, "Found while testing", item 2).

## Proposed next step
Pass `-project_path $RepoRoot` to `ec` (or `Push-Location $RepoRoot` around the lane), so the build, `finish_freezing` and the executable all use the same folder.

comments.body: Fixed in `920ffba` (PR #58).

issue.title: Run every test-matrix lane from the repository root
issue.body:
Refs #55

`ec` writes `EIFGENs` to the current folder, but the script ran `finish_freezing` and `xpact_tests.exe` under the repository root. Started from another folder, it relinked stale code and ran the tests outside the repository; a test printed `FAIL`, the exe still exited 0 (#45), and the script said `ok`. Now every lane runs inside `Push-Location $RepoRoot`, and the caller's folder is restored in `finally`. (`ec -project_path` alone was not enough: the tests read repository files relative to the current folder.)

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| From `%TEMP%\xpact-issue55-cwd` | stale relink, `FAIL` printed, `matrix: ok`, exit 0 (or `Cobj1.o: No such file`, exit 1) | built and tested in the repo, no `EIFGENs` outside, exit 0 |
| From the repository root | ok | ok |

CI is not affected: Jenkins starts in the workspace root.

Report with verification and logs: [reports/issue-0055/report.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/55-project-path/reports/issue-0055/report.md)

issue.title: Advance past a CR in the first loop of normalized_input
issue.body:
Refs #28

**Parser change, one line** (`src/xp_parser.e`, `normalized_input`): a CR set `l_needs_copy` but did not advance `i`, so the loop variant `a_input.count - i + 1` did not decrease and every input containing a CR failed with assertions on. Now `i := i + 1`, as the second loop already does. No contract changed or switched off. The repair is the one proposed in `reports/issue-0028/proposed-repair.diff` on 2026-10-21; the student approved committing it.

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Test matrix, assertions on (Workbench, Finalized) | `normalized_input` loop variant, exit 1 | CR test passes; stops at the known B03 postcondition (#3), exit 1 |
| Test matrix, assertions off | ok | ok |
| W3C, assertions on | 270 passed, 1,360 crashes | **1,444 passed, 47 crashes** |
| W3C, assertions off | 1,491 passed, 236 failed | unchanged |

The 47 remaining crashes were hidden behind this bug; all are in DTD declaration parsing (`parse_attlist_declaration`, `parse_content_particle`, `parse_attlist_default_value`, `put_external_entity`). Listed, not repaired here.

Report with verification and logs: [reports/issue-0028/report.md#repair-2026-10-22](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/28-cr-loop-variant/reports/issue-0028/report.md#repair-2026-10-22)

milestone.title: Week 3 - Failure reporting
milestone.description: How the test runner reports failure; a deliberately failing test (B01, B02). A bounded fix or a precise proposal with evidence.

issue.body:
## Steps to reproduce
1. Run the assertions-on workbench lane (see the B03 finding).
2. Compare the tests reported before the failure in `test_garbage_collection_suspension` with the list of all tests.

## Expected
Every test runs. Failures are counted and reported at the end.

## Actual
In the baseline from 2026-10-14, the run stopped at the B03 contract violation, so the tests after it did not run in the assertions-on lanes. Their status is unknown.

## Logs
Original logs: `student/baseline/logs/matrix-workbench.log`, `matrix-finalized-keep.log`.
Attach the list of tests that ran and the list of tests that exist.

## Notes
Related to B01 / B02 (failure reporting) and B04 (report crashes and incomplete runs separately).

## Update 2026-10-22
Still true after the #28 repair: with assertions on, the run stops in `test_garbage_collection_suspension` (B03, #3), test 35 of 42 in `XP_TEST_ROOT.make`, so the last 7 tests do not run.

comments.body: Fixed in `aff0584` (PR #61). With assertions on, all 42 tests run; B03 is recorded with its trace.

issue.title: Record an exception in one test and run the remaining tests
issue.body:
Refs #60

`XP_TEST_ROOT.make` called its 42 tests directly; the first exception ended the run. With assertions on that is B03 (#3) in test 35, so 7 tests never ran. Now each test goes through `run_test`: its `rescue` records the failure, prints `FAIL: <test> raised an exception` and the exception trace, and `retry` skips to the next test. No test changed.

| Lane | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Assertions on (Workbench, Finalized) | stops in test 35, exit 1 | B03 recorded with trace, `42 run, 1 raised an exception`, exit 1 |
| Assertions off | ok | ok |

The end of the run is unchanged (`check tests_passed: False end`), so with assertions off a failure still exits 0; that is B01 (#45), next.

Report with verification and logs: [reports/issue-0060/report.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/60-runner-continues/reports/issue-0060/report.md)

issue.title: Exit nonzero when a test failed, in every build (B01)
issue.body:
Refs #45

B01. Both Eiffel test runners (`XP_TEST_ROOT`, `XP_NATIVE_RUNTIME_SMOKE`) ended with `check ...: False end`, which only fires when assertions are compiled in. With assertions off, a failing test printed `FAIL` and the exe exited 0, so `run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1`, `run_native_runtime_smoke.ps1` and Jenkins said ok. Now they print `... FAILED` and call `{EXCEPTIONS}.die (1)`.

With a temporary deliberately failing assert (not committed; B02 adds a permanent switchable one):

| Lane | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Off / Workbench, Off / Finalized | `FAIL` printed, `matrix: ok`, **exit 0** | `FAILED`, exit 1 |
| On / Workbench, On / Finalized (`-keep`) | - | exit 1 |
| native smoke Off | `FAIL` printed, **exit 0** | exit 1 |
| native smoke On | - | exit 1 |

Without it: assertions-off lanes and both native smoke runs `ok`, exit 0; assertions-on lanes exit 1 on the real B03 failure (#3).

Report: [reports/issue-0045/report.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/45-nonzero-exit/reports/issue-0045/report.md) · logs: `student/results/B01-nonzero-exit/`

Revert after merge: `git revert <squash sha>`

issue.title: Add a switchable deliberately failing meta-test (B02)
issue.body:
Refs #46

B02. A meta-test that fails on demand, without touching any real test:

| `XPACT_META_FAIL` | `xpact_tests.exe` | native runtime smoke |
|---|---|---|
| `assert` / `1` | failed `assert` in `test_meta_deliberate_failure` | failed `assert` |
| `exception` | the test raises (the #60 rescue path) | failed `assert` |
| unset | nothing | nothing |

| Configuration | `assert` | `exception` | unset |
|---|---|---|---|
| Off / Workbench, Off / Finalized | exit 1 | exit 1 | ok, 0 |
| On / Workbench, On / Finalized (`-keep`) | exit 1 | exit 1 | exit 1 (B03, #3) |
| native smoke Off, On | exit 1 | - | ok, 0 |

The wrappers report every failure (`Test executable failed for ...`, `Native runtime smoke failed for ...`). **Jenkins not checked** (no server here): the stage runs `run_eiffel_test_matrix.ps1`, which inherits the job environment; to confirm, set `XPACT_META_FAIL=assert` on one Jenkins run.

Also: `student/GUIDE.md` and `student/PLAN.md` updated for B01, B02, #28, #48 and #60 (the GUIDE still said the finalized lane has no `-keep`).

Report: [reports/issue-0046/report.md](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/fix/46-meta-tests/reports/issue-0046/report.md) · logs: `student/results/B02-meta-tests/`

Refs #68

## What
A01 was ticked done (#18), but three items of its "Done when" list had no evidence. This adds them. Docs and evidence only; no source or test change.

- **Tests linked:** `ok.xml` → `test_well_formed_callbacks` (`tests/xp_test_root.e:72`), `rejected.xml` → `test_mismatched_tag_is_rejected` (`tests/xp_test_root.e:92`); parser path `XP_PARSER.close_element` (`src/xp_parser.e:3852`).

| `ok.xml` (control) | ACCEPT, 7 events | ACCEPT, 7 events (same as 2026-10-15) | ✅ |

commit.message:
Fix the loop variant in direct_start_tag_attributes (B03)

The outer loop's variant a_end_index - i does not decrease when an
iteration only sets l_valid to False, as at the '/' of "<root/>", so
with assertions on the runtime raised "Non-decreasing loop variant".
Under GC suspension MEMORY.execute_without_collection swallowed that
exception, which surfaced as the final_finished_or_suspended
postcondition failure in test_garbage_collection_suspension.

Count the l_valid exit as progress: a_end_index - i +
l_valid.to_integer. Behaviour is unchanged and the check stays on.

Verified: all four test matrix cells print "xpact Phase 1 tests: ok",
exit 0; see reports/fix-report-issue-3.md for the diagnostics.

commit.message:
Add a regression test for the CR loop variant in normalized_input

With assertions on, every input that contains a CR stops in
XP_PARSER.normalized_input with a non-decreasing loop variant. No test
caught it, because only a handler that wants no events reaches that loop.
The new test uses XP_NULL_EVENT_HANDLER and parses five CR cases.

Assertions off: the test passes. Assertions on: the test fails with the
loop variant, so it catches the bug. With the one-line repair applied
locally (not committed) it passes. Logs in reports/issue-0028/.

Refs #28 (also opened as pull request #31)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make the W3C harness tests pass on Python 3.10

Before Python 3.11 the csv module cannot write NUL, so write_reports
failed with "need to escape" when a message contained one. NUL now
becomes ? in results.tsv, as it already did in junit.xml. The test
also checks the TSV text, so it catches the bug on every version.

Tested: 22 tests OK on Python 3.10.22 and 3.15.0. Logs in
reports/issue-0032/.

issue.body:
## Problem
Jenkins (`ci/Jenkinsfile.windows-phase1`, run on `main` @ `9e1747d`, 2026-10-23) stops in stage **Build Eiffel-Backed DLL**; every later stage is skipped and the build is FAILURE.

## Environment
Jenkins machine: EiffelStudio 25.02.9.8723 Enterprise (win64), VS 2022 Build Tools (cl 19.44), Windows 11. Not reproducible on the student PC as is (there the 25.12 Standard path exists).

## Command
`scripts\build_native_eiffel.ps1` (Jenkins stage "Build Eiffel-Backed DLL")

## Expected / actual
- Expected: the script finds the Eiffel runtime include folder, as it did before the student fixes (`C:\El2502E\studio\spec\win64\include`).
- Actual: `Cannot find Eiffel runtime include directory.` at `scripts\build_native_eiffel.ps1:46`

## Cause — confirmed from the code
`9eb18bd` (#2) **replaced** the fallback `C:\El2502E\...` (EiffelStudio 25.02 Enterprise, the Jenkins install) with `C:\Program Files\Eiffel Software\EiffelStudio 25.12 Standard\...` (the student PC) instead of adding it. `20e6bc3` (#10, #11) did the same in `scripts\run_native_runtime_smoke.ps1:40`. `ISE_EIFFEL` is evidently not set on Jenkins (otherwise it would be used first) — suspected, not seen.

## Fix (planned)
In both scripts, search in order: `ISE_EIFFEL`, `C:\El2502E`, EiffelStudio 25.12 Standard, then the EiffelStudio that provides `ec` on `PATH`. Error message lists the folders searched.

## Done when
- [ ] Both scripts search the list above
- [ ] Order tested with a temporary copy of the function and fake install folders
- [ ] `build_native_eiffel.ps1` and `run_native_runtime_smoke.ps1` still build on the student PC
- [ ] Jenkins log saved in `reports/issue-NNNN/`; report with verification
- [ ] Jenkins rerun gets past the include lookup (needs the supervisor)

issue.body:
For the supervisor to compare and merge. **Do not merge from the student side.**

## What this brings into `main`

Since PR #72 (23 Oct), `student-Mass` has **one** new commit:

| Commit | Change | Issue |
|---|---|---|

Full report: [`reports/issue-0073/report.md`](https://github.com/andersoxie/xpact/blob/student-Mass/reports/issue-0073/report.md)

- [ ] **A Jenkins run** that gets past "Build Eiffel-Backed DLL". Only you can start one. #73 stays open until then.

issue.title: Finding: parser fails 283 W3C cases and the DLL tests (#38, #39, #40, K3); Jenkins FAILURE on main

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: type:finding
labels.description: Something observed that is wrong or surprising

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Must be solved first

labels.description: Tests, test runs and test tools

issue.body:
**1. Problem:** the Jenkins build of `main` at `cf12dee` (2026-10-23) ends in FAILURE at the W3C XML conformance check: 236 wrong verdicts in both finalized builds and 47 crashes with assertions on. The DLL tests from #37 also show #38 (start-tag shortcut skips parsing), #39 (invalid UTF-8 accepted) and #40 (crash when a chunk ends with `<`), and the assertions DLL smoke test crashes (K3, draft 07).

**2. Environment:** Jenkins (EiffelStudio 25.02 Enterprise, VS 2022) and the student PC (EiffelStudio 25.12 Standard, VS 18) give identical W3C totals.

**3. Command:** `scripts\run_benchmarks.ps1 -EiffelBuild Finalized,FinalizedAssertions` (Jenkins "Benchmarks" stage).

**4. Expected:** every applicable W3C case (1,727 per build) passes; no crashes.

**5. Actual:** Finalized 1,491 passed / 236 failed; FinalizedAssertions 1,444 passed / 236 failed / 47 errors.

**6. Error output:** `W3C XML conformance failed` (`run_benchmarks.ps1:597`), `Finished: FAILURE`.

**7. Investigation / 8. Cause (confirmed per case by the fix):** no UTF-8 decoding (characters checked per byte, names accepted any byte > 127), no UTF-16 support, DTD declarations without required-space and keyword checks, loops whose error branches do not advance (contract failures under assertions), the #38 shortcut also running on the final call, and smaller WFC/validity mix-ups.

**9. Fix / 10. Verification:** in the linked PR and `reports/issue-NNNN/report.md`.

commit.message:
Fix parser conformance: strict UTF-8, UTF-16, names and DTD declarations

Decode UTF-8 strictly and check XML Char; convert UTF-16 with a BOM and
declared ISO-8859-1/US-ASCII; apply the fifth-edition name rules in
scan_name; check required spaces, attribute types, groups, mixed content
and trailing content in DTD declarations; make DTD loops advance on error
(47 assertion crashes); allow empty system literals; skip comments and PIs
when scanning the DOCTYPE; fix comments, PI targets, char refs, attribute
spacing, version numbers, namespaces, entity balance and normalization.
W3C: 1,727 of 1,727 applicable cases pass in both finalized builds.

Refs #79

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix the start-tag shortcut and UTF-16 decoder loops in the DLL layer

The direct start-tag shortcut now only runs on non-final calls, so a final
call parses all input (#38). The UTF-16 decoders advance on error, which
fixes the assertions DLL smoke crash (K3). The parser is told the DLL layer
converts input to UTF-8 itself, so it is not converted twice.

Refs #79

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read an empty conformance file as an empty document

Two W3C cases are empty files; the harness exited with code 2 instead of
letting the parser reject them.

Refs #79

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add a known-failures list to the W3C conformance runner

Listed failures stay visible in the reports but do not fail the run; new
failures and listed cases that change still do. The list is empty after
the parser fixes. Six new runner tests.

Refs #79

Record the #79 fix report and evidence

issue.title: Correct Jenkins native libexpat failure classification and exit status
issue.body:
Jenkins build 67 compiled the native suite, then CTest reported `***Exception: SegFault`. The adapter labelled any nonzero result as expected whenever the expected-failure list was nonempty, while leaving CTest's exit code 8 active for the Jenkins wrapper. This produced a reassuring message followed by a failed stage.

Require a complete upstream test summary, reconcile its failure count, and match every observed failure against the expected source/name patterns. Resolve declaration sources from the manifest because assertions can originate in shared helpers. Reject crashes, incomplete output, ambiguous tests, setup/teardown failures, and unlisted failures. Print verbose CTest output, replace the previous run's log before build preparation, fail on log persistence errors, and restore the process environment. Clear LASTEXITCODE only after validating an accepted result.

Add six orchestration regression tests and run them in both Jenkins pipelines. Update the adapter and parity documentation to distinguish expected-failure metadata from observed test outcomes.

Validation: all six behavioral tests passed under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, including failure/retry sequences, native exit-code propagation, helper-source attribution, stale logs, failed log persistence, and environment restoration. Full-adapter checks with real installed CTest verified child exit 1 -> CTest 8 -> accepted wrapper exit 0, plus complete-pass handling. The saved build-67 crash log is now rejected explicitly. `git diff --check` passed.

The underlying native crash remains unresolved. Diagnostic runs also found failures and a GC crash after excluding allocator tests; callback assertions using longjmp across Eiffel frames strongly implicate invalid GC roots. This PR corrects reporting and acceptance criteria. The full native suite and Jenkins pipeline have not passed.

issue.title: Isolate Windows libexpat tests to contain callback assertion failures
issue.body:
Jenkins builds 67 and 68 crash before finishing the native suite. Minicheck uses longjmp for assertions, including assertions inside C callbacks entered from Eiffel. Controlled sequences showed that a callback failure could leave invalid Eiffel GC roots for a later parser setup; correcting the Jenkins result classification exposed this existing crash.

Run each registered Windows test in a fresh child process. Assertion failures print the named test and fixture phase, flush diagnostics, and exit the child immediately. Passing tests still run all 12 chunk-size/deferral combinations; a failing named test stops at its first assertion. The parent collects results and continues with a fresh process. Capture all three upstream registration APIs and reconcile their metadata against the enabled upstream suite.

Use an atomically assigned Windows job to release the active child when the parent is cancelled. Bound child execution at 120 seconds by default and the CTest suite at 1800 seconds. Confirm termination before continuing after a timeout; abort without a completed-run summary if cleanup cannot be confirmed. Keep crashes, timeouts, and unlisted failures fatal. Stream CTest output to Jenkins while retaining the saved log. Non-Windows builds retain the original runner.

Add native lifecycle regression tests and run them with the existing adapter tests in both Jenkins pipelines. Document the fail-fast context coverage and current parity limits.

Validation:
- Built the real Expat 2.8.1 suite with VS2022/MSVC against the Jenkins workspace library; the registry covers all 399 enabled tests.
- The real test_invalid_foreign_dtd -> test_attributes sequence now completes with one assertion failure and one pass, without a process exception.
- Real CTest with an expected allocator failure plus a passing test returns CTest 8 and a validated PowerShell wrapper status 0.
- All 12 adapter/isolation regression tests passed. Native tests cover callback exit, later-test state, setup/teardown phases, real access violations, timeouts, cancellation, and child release. Native tests passed again after cleanup changes.
- A deliberately bounded diagnostic sweep (five seconds per child) completed all 399 named tests in 87 seconds: 267 passed, 121 assertions, 11 timeouts, zero process exceptions. This short diagnostic limit is distinct from the configured 120-second gate.
- git diff --check passed.

The full native suite still has unlisted compatibility failures. This change contains the harness crash and provides complete named results; it does not establish a passing Jenkins pipeline or change the expected-failure patterns.

issue.title: Fix libexpat native failures and parsing timeouts
issue.body:
Jenkins rejected the Windows libexpat gate on native crashes, unexpected compatibility failures, and parsing timeouts. The rebuilt DLL now completes all 399 upstream Expat 2.8.1 tests: 361 pass and 38 match the existing allocator-injection expectations. The Windows PowerShell 5.1 gate returns 0; the expected-failure list and timeout limits are unchanged.

The fixes cover native buffer/reset/error lifecycles, strong ownership of Eiffel parser handles, caller-owned content models, partial encodings, callback positions and literal default output, and external-child declarations across prefix replay. Iterative entity/model traversal and bounded token scans remove stack and repeated-scanning failures. Silent completed DTDs can be reused with source comparison, accounting restoration, and invalidation; external replay retains detached declaration deltas instead of child parsers.

The adapter now applies each test's actual deferral configuration to parser creation and reset. Native names use the approved 512 KiB ceiling and native tokens stay within the existing 10 MiB input budget. Document depth, attribute, nested-expansion, and expansion-byte limits remain bounded; generic Eiffel name/token defaults and fifth-edition name rules are preserved.

Validation:
- Full Jenkins-equivalent native gate: 399 completed in 380.9 seconds; 361 pass, 38 expected allocator assertions, no unexpected failures/crashes/timeouts. Child timeout 120 seconds; suite timeout 1800 seconds.
- Clean production and assertion DLL builds and expanded C lifecycle smoke suites pass.
- Four Eiffel matrix cells: 52 tests each, 208 executions pass.
- W3C finalized and assertion builds: 1,727 applicable cases pass per build, 858 skipped, zero failures/errors.
- 13 adapter and 28 W3C-runner Python regressions pass; Windows public/bridge ABI smokes pass.
- Native callback benchmark produces the same 3,020 events across ten documents with parser creation and parser reuse.

Changes are separated into adapter configuration, C lifecycle, GC ownership, and parser compatibility commits.

issue.title: Add WSL2 GCC benchmarks and xpact compiler comparison
issue.body:
The existing benchmark lane builds xpact with Windows EiffelStudio/MSVC, while its direct C libexpat comparison runs through WSL. Add a separate lane that builds xpact with Linux EiffelStudio/GCC and measures both executables inside Linux, excluding Windows-to-WSL startup overhead.

The runner isolates each Eiffel build mode, verifies the generated GCC compiler, records versions and flags, and invalidates measured reports before rebuilding. Failed builds, benchmark failures and report-write failures cannot leave a previous successful measurement presented as the new result.

- Add a PowerShell WSL2 wrapper and portable Python runner for finalized, finalized-with-assertions and optional workbench builds, including normal and suspended GC.
- Make the benchmark ECF portable and conditionalize the Windows Base precompile.
- Add an opt-in Jenkins stage to both pipelines and run the new orchestration tests in GitHub Actions.
- Document the same-computer xpact comparison and commit its 24 raw repetitions. Finalized throughput was 13.629 MiB/s on MSVC versus 12.400 on WSL/GCC with assertions off, and 1.434 versus 1.535 with assertions on. These results include OS/runtime differences and do not isolate the C compiler.

### Validation

- 14 new lifecycle/timing tests pass on Windows Python 3.14 and WSL Python 3.8.
- All 28 existing W3C harness tests pass on Windows.
- Actual WSL2 builds and timings completed for all three Eiffel modes: 10,000 documents, one warmup and three measured repetitions per variant.
- Fresh MSVC finalized builds and timings completed with assertions off/on and normal/suspended GC.
- PowerShell syntax, Python compilation, raw comparison workload consistency and staged whitespace checks pass.

The committed WSL runner uses the distribution's libexpat for its C baseline; the published compiler-comparison snapshot concerns xpact itself. Live Jenkins execution remains unverified; the new lane defaults to disabled and requires Linux EiffelStudio configured for the Jenkins account.

The runner isolates each Eiffel build mode, verifies the generated GCC compiler, records versions and flags, and invalidates measured reports before rebuilding. Failed builds, benchmark failures and report-write failures cannot leave a previous successful measurement presented as the new result.

- Add a PowerShell WSL2 wrapper and portable Python runner for finalized, finalized-with-assertions and optional workbench builds, including normal and suspended GC.
- Make the benchmark ECF portable and conditionalize the Windows Base precompile.
- Add an opt-in Jenkins stage to both pipelines and run the new orchestration tests in GitHub Actions.
- Document the same-computer xpact comparison and commit its 24 raw repetitions. Finalized throughput was 13.629 MiB/s on MSVC versus 12.400 on WSL/GCC with assertions off, and 1.434 versus 1.535 with assertions on. These results include OS/runtime differences and do not isolate the C compiler.

### Validation

- 14 new lifecycle/timing tests pass on Windows Python 3.14 and WSL Python 3.8.
- All 28 existing W3C harness tests pass on Windows.
- Actual WSL2 builds and timings completed for all three Eiffel modes: 10,000 documents, one warmup and three measured repetitions per variant.
- Fresh MSVC finalized builds and timings completed with assertions off/on and normal/suspended GC.
- PowerShell syntax, Python compilation, raw comparison workload consistency and staged whitespace checks pass.

The committed WSL runner uses the distribution's libexpat for its C baseline; the published compiler-comparison snapshot concerns xpact itself. Live Jenkins execution remains unverified; the new lane defaults to disabled and requires Linux EiffelStudio configured for the Jenkins account.

issue.title: Improve tag dispatch with cached markup markers
issue.body:
Ordinary marker strings in `XP_PARSER.parse_markup` were recreated on every dispatch: 909 temporary marker constructions per 100-item catalog document. Cache the ten marker literals with Eiffel `once` strings while preserving the original classification order, diagnostics and contracts. This retains the catalog improvement without the earlier byte-dispatch prototype's text-heavy regression.

Same-computer, fresh baseline/candidate finalized builds against `3a5551d`, six alternating AB/BA pairs per workload:

| Workload | Windows MSVC throughput change | WSL2 GCC throughput change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Catalog | +31.3% | +29.6% |
| Text-heavy | −0.7% | +0.3% |
| Attribute-heavy | +0.6% | +0.1% |
| PubMed extract | −1.5% | +0.8% |
| Unicode stylesheet | +13.5% | +9.0% |
| Legislation | −0.3% | +0.3% |

Both text-heavy medians meet the preselected 2% regression budget. Assertion-enabled catalog throughput improves by 6.7% on MSVC and 4.1% on GCC. Small changes remain within observed pair variation; the real corpora show that marker reuse does not remove the remaining parsing bottlenecks.

Adds a reusable paired benchmark driver with common iteration calibration, child-result validation, executable/input hashes and report cleanup after failure. Documents the method and all 84 raw pairs, including outliers, in `docs/tag-dispatch-performance.md` and `benchmarks/results/`.

Validation:

- All 54 Eiffel regression tests pass in each workbench/finalized × assertions off/on lane. New cases verify malformed-prefix diagnostics, callback positions and repeated failure/recovery with DTD state reset.
- Fresh baseline/candidate match on 1,727 applicable W3C cases and 40 directed cases in each finalized assertion mode; 858 cases are excluded by the existing profile. No outcome or diagnostic differences.
- Rebuilt Eiffel-backed Windows DLL passes the native smoke test.
- All 52 Python harness tests pass on Windows; the ten new paired-driver tests also pass on WSL Python 3.8. Includes direct and hard-link input/output collision checks. Adds the new suite to GitHub Actions.

The cached strings are bounded, runtime-managed constants. Prefix helpers only read them and retain no parser or document references, so reset and failure add no cache invalidation or resource cleanup path.

issue.title: Add email notifications for failed and unstable xpact builds
issue.body:
Neither xpact Jenkinsfile currently sends email when a build fails or becomes unstable.

Add an `EMAIL_RECIPIENTS` parameter to both pipelines so addresses can be entered in Jenkins without committing them to the repository. Start with an empty default, retain the last submitted value for later builds, and allow clearing it to disable notifications.

Send one notification for final `FAILURE` and `UNSTABLE` results, after artifact/test publication. Include the build result and links to the build and console. Do not send for success, aborted, or not-built results. Mail delivery errors must preserve the original build result, and cancellation must propagate.

Local verification already passed 19 Groovy stub scenarios against both complete Jenkinsfiles, covering recipient lifecycle, result filtering, message contents, publication ordering, SMTP failures, and interruption propagation. No email was sent. Real Jenkins Declarative/CPS execution and SMTP delivery remain unverified.

Full-file validation also exposed two pre-existing Groovy escaping errors in the all-tests Sonar PowerShell block. A minimal prerequisite correction is included separately so that pipeline can parse and be tested.

There was no pinned, independently verifiable build path for comparing our parser with Finnian Reilly's Xpact-core. issue.title: Found and fixed a **Windows Git path-length problem**.
issue.body:
Jenkins’ longer workspace path caused 11 setup-test errors:

```text
Filename too long
fatal: bad object HEAD
```

This stopped the dual comparison before either parser ran. The regular W3C checks later passed all 1,727 applicable cases in both assertion modes.

The [fix](/C:/Users/ander/Documents/xpact/scripts/prepare_xpact_core.py:64) enables `core.longpaths=true` per Git command, without changing global settings. A regression reproduces the original failure with a 270-character path.

**All 141 affected tests pass locally.** Changes are uncommitted; Jenkins has not been rerun. The HTTP 403 history warnings are separate and nonfatal.

commit.message:
Found and fixed a **Windows Git path-length problem**.

Jenkins’ longer workspace path caused 11 setup-test errors:

```text
Filename too long
fatal: bad object HEAD
```

This stopped the dual comparison before either parser ran. The regular W3C checks later passed all 1,727 applicable cases in both assertion modes.

The [fix](/C:/Users/ander/Documents/xpact/scripts/prepare_xpact_core.py:64) enables `core.longpaths=true` per Git command, without changing global settings. A regression reproduces the original failure with a 270-character path.

**All 141 affected tests pass locally.** Changes are uncommitted; Jenkins has not been rerun. The HTTP 403 history warnings are separate and nonfatal.

commit.message:
Found and fixed a **Windows Git path-length problem**.

Jenkins’ longer workspace path caused 11 setup-test errors:

```text
Filename too long
fatal: bad object HEAD
```

This stopped the dual comparison before either parser ran. The regular W3C checks later passed all 1,727 applicable cases in both assertion modes.

The [fix](/C:/Users/ander/Documents/xpact/scripts/prepare_xpact_core.py:64) enables `core.longpaths=true` per Git command, without changing global settings. A regression reproduces the original failure with a 270-character path.

**All 141 affected tests pass locally.** Changes are uncommitted; Jenkins has not been rerun. The HTTP 403 history warnings are separate and nonfatal.
